clue.text: No end of bitter — beer drunk by more mature writer

indicators.note: no end of tells us to drop the final letter of the word meaning bitter

parts.note: a bitter wind or winter is a hard one

indicators.note: something drunk by a person goes inside them, so the beer sits inside the word for more mature

parts.note: more mature means older
a pint is a measure of beer, standing for the drink itself

explanation.surface: A grumpy older man downs a pint of beer while complaining about bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' looks like the beer, but it is an adjective meaning harsh; 'No end of' and 'drunk by' are the two operations.
explanation.definitionFit: The playwright behind The Birthday Party and The Caretaker, a Nobel laureate in literature, is a writer.

clue.text: Cooler top displayed by rider in arena

parts.note: A1, written here as AI, means first-rate or top

indicators.note: in places the proviso word within the arena word

parts.note: a ring is an arena for boxing or circus acts
a rider is a condition or proviso added to an agreement

explanation.surface: A top horse rider shows off in the arena on a hot day, wanting cooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' gives A1, with the figure 1 read as the letter I. 'Rider' is a clause added to a contract, not a horseman.
explanation.definitionFit: A system that chills the air in a building or car is a cooler for its occupants.

clue.text: Colour of brooch — red in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone describes the colour of a red brooch, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment, so it is a colour.

clue.text: Chuck away fish and suet-based dish

parts.note: to chuck away rubbish is to dump it
the ling is a long food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A cook throws out the fish and serves a suet pudding instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A small ball of suet dough boiled in a stew is a classic British suet-based dish.

clue.text: I have meal beneath the moon

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath means the eating word comes below the moon's name

parts.note: Io is one of the moons of Jupiter
to dine is to have a meal

explanation.surface: Someone describes eating dinner outdoors under the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single letter 'I', the chemical symbol for the element, disguised as the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: In the periodic table, the halogen element with atomic number 53 has the symbol I.

clue.text: Soldiers get through chocolate stocked in Spanish cafés

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve soldiers

indicators.note: stocked in means the sweet is held inside the word for get through

parts.note: to get through an exam is to pass it
a bar is a slab of chocolate

explanation.surface: Troops on leave munch through chocolate bought from Spanish cafés.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve; 'stocked in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish bars serving small snack dishes are the cafés of Spain where people graze in the evening.

clue.text: Badly run USA lotteries risky enterprise

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the following words are arranged poorly, i.e. jumbled

explanation.surface: Poorly managed American lotteries are a gamble in themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges RUN, USA and LOTTERIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The deadly revolver game of chance is used figuratively for any reckless gamble or dangerous venture.

clue.text: Page penned by French philosopher in part of uni

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, as in a pen, so the page letter sits inside the philosopher

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French existentialist philosopher and novelist

explanation.surface: A page written by a French thinker is studied in a university department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing, but it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds and buildings of a university make up its site, one part of the institution.

clue.text: Group of pupils succeeded, taking first of test papers

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word test

parts.note: a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A class of students passed after sitting the opening test paper.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools, a set of pupils grouped by ability is called by this name.

clue.text: Fellow giving a form of support to poor actor

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
a ham is an overacting, poor actor

explanation.surface: A man offers some kind of backing to a struggling actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor actor' suggests pity, but it is a ham, a bad performer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament patriarch's name is a man's first name, so it can stand for a fellow.

clue.text: Amount of money is hidden over in warehouse

indicators.note: hidden here means tucked inside the storage word

parts.note: a depot is a storage building or warehouse

indicators.note: over means the little word is turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone describes a sum of cash secretly stashed in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like a hidden-word signal, but here it puts the turned-round 'is' (signalled by 'over') inside the storage word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum paid up front as security or put into a bank account is a deposit of money.

clue.text: Writing by poet, initially something flowery

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word poet

parts.note: a rose is a flower, something flowery

explanation.surface: A poet's first effort is flowery writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowery' suggests ornate style, but it just means a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary written language, not verse, is a form of writing.

clue.text: Left joined with Labour leader in team producing electoral victory

parts.note: and joins things, standing for joined with

indicators.note: in places the leader letter inside the team word

parts.note: a side is a team

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word Labour

explanation.surface: Left-wingers unite with the Labour leader's team to win an election.
explanation.walkthrough: The L from 'Labour leader' goes inside SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An overwhelming majority in a general election is called by the name of a collapsing hillside.

clue.text: 11 dispatched with coin enclosed

indicators.note: enclosed means the coin is placed inside the word for dispatched

parts.note: something dispatched has been sent
a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: An item from clue 11 is posted with a coin inside the envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' refers to the answer of 11 across, DEPOSIT, in its sense of material settling out.
explanation.definitionFit: Matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid is a deposit in the geological sense.

clue.text: Courier taking motorway near city to north of Germany

indicators.note: in a down clue, to the north of means placed above, so the city precedes the country

parts.note: M is a motorway, as in the M1
Essen is a city in the Ruhr, western Germany

explanation.surface: A courier drives the motorway near a city in northern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carries messages or parcels is a courier, a bearer of dispatches.

clue.text: Mother captures wild beast, showing lots of bottle

indicators.note: captures means the mother word holds the animal inside it

parts.note: mam is a dialect word for mother
a gnu, or wildebeest, is a wild African antelope

explanation.surface: A brave mother catches a wild animal, showing great courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like British slang for courage, but here it is a real wine bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-size wine bottle holds a lot, about one and a half litres.

clue.text: I forage about, finding truffles ultimately for pâté

indicators.note: about means the letters go round and are put in a new order
ultimately picks the last letter of the word truffles

explanation.surface: A pig roots around hunting truffles for a luxury pâté.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I FORAGE; the S from 'truffles ultimately' ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rich liver of a fattened goose or duck is served as a French pâté.

clue.text: Component of fertiliser makes path so slippery

indicators.note: slippery suggests the letters slide out of place into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's fertiliser makes the garden path slippery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippery' rearranges PATH SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A potassium compound from wood ash is a key ingredient of plant food.

clue.text: Very good hollows for birds

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means very good in crosswords
pits are hollows in the ground

explanation.surface: Holes in the ground make fine nesting spots for birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Small brown songbirds of meadows and moorland, such as the tree and meadow kinds, are birds.

clue.text: Film shows Blair's expelling New Labour opponent

indicators.note: expelling means the letter for new is thrown out

parts.note: Tony Blair, so Blair's is Tony's
a Tory, a Conservative, opposes the Labour Party

explanation.surface: A film shows Tony Blair throwing a Conservative out of New Labour.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair led the Labour Party, rebranded New Labour; dropping N from TONY'S leaves TOYS.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1995 Pixar animation about toys coming alive was the first fully computer-animated feature.

clue.text: Republican enemy trounced one finally

indicators.note: finally puts the letter for one at the end
trounced means beaten up, so the letters are knocked into disorder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Republican beat the enemy at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican' looks like the US party, but it means a citizen of the Republic of Yemen.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the Republic of Yemen on the Arabian peninsula belongs to a republic.

clue.text: Page with question and answer? Right, nothing more

parts.note: O, the round zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A quiz sheet with a question and answer, and nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: A book size made by folding a sheet twice into four leaves names the page format.

clue.text: Get journalist involved in course of action

indicators.note: involved means the journalist is wrapped up inside the word for get

parts.note: to procure something is to get it
ed, an editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Bring in a reporter to decide what to do next.
explanation.definitionFit: An established way of doing something is a set method, a course of action.

clue.text: Recalled African country introducing school for religion

indicators.note: introducing means the school letter is brought inside
recalled means called back, so the country name is read backwards

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: An African nation's recalled envoy opens a religious school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns MALI into ILAM; 'introducing' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The monotheistic faith founded on the Qur'an is one of the world's major religions.

clue.text: Metal block in grotto, oddly

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word grotto

explanation.surface: A block of metal found in a cave, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like an anagram signal, but it takes letters 1, 3 and 5 of GROTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast bar of gold or other metal is a block of it.

clue.text: Set off, heading for Tasmania by boat

indicators.note: heading for picks the first letter of the word Tasmania

parts.note: a rigger is a ship with rigging, as in a square-rigger

explanation.surface: Someone sets out by boat, bound for Tasmania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like travel, but it takes the head letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger an alarm or a reaction is to set it off.

clue.text: Trendy bachelor snubs English resort

indicators.note: snubs means the bachelor is cut out and left off

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on the south coast of England

explanation.surface: A fashionable single man turns his nose up at a seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up to date or bang on fashion is an informal sense of being trendy.

clue.text: Dog to proceed across road, then winding street

indicators.note: across means the proceed phrase stretches over and around the road letters

parts.note: to go on is to proceed

indicators.note: winding means the letters twist into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog crosses the road, then wanders down a winding street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts GO ON either side of RD; 'winding' rearranges STREET into SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-tan Scottish gundog breed is a kind of dog.
